wiki-iran.standing: The Wikipedia article on Iran, and how many people read it each day. A country page of this size has a steady baseline of students and browsers, so the daily count only jumps when something happens that sends people looking for context.
wiki-iran.recent: Readership tracked a sixth month of war reaching the Gulf's shipping lanes. The 25 August peak came as Washington widened sanctions to isolate Iran's economy; attention held through the US strike on Larak Island, Tehran's retaliation, eight missiles intercepted over Jordan, and a drone downed offshore by the United Arab Emirates.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent rose 3% to $90.97 as the US and Iran exchanged attacks: Iran struck two US airbases in Jordan, the UAE intercepted a drone, and a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Trump also posted a fake video of the Kharg Island terminal exploding. The war premium sits on a series still 13% below its Jul 23 high of $105.30.

wti.standing: The US crude benchmark, priced at the Cushing, Oklahoma storage hub and the reference for most oil produced in North America. It sets what refiners pay for a barrel, and petrol, diesel and freight costs follow it.
wti.recent: Crude has fallen roughly 16% since early June, but the last week pushed the other way: Brent rose 3% to $90.97 after US strikes on Iran and Tehran's response, a war premium on the risk of disruption rather than any lost cargo. The other supply story is Venezuela, where Washington took a stake in 65 billion barrels of reserves.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for a million British thermal units of natural gas, set at a pipeline hub in Louisiana. It prices American power generation, home heating and the LNG cargoes the US ships abroad, and fertiliser and industrial costs follow it.
natgas-hh.recent: US gas has drifted down about 9% over the window even as the rest of the world tightened: EU storage sits near 64%, Delhi raised compressed natural gas ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg on surging global LNG prices, and Pakistan apologized for night-time blackouts after a delayed cargo. Henry Hub is a domestic price, and it is not following.

wheat.standing: The world price of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. It moves on harvests, export policy and war in the growing regions, and bread, flour and animal feed move after it.
wheat.recent: Wheat has climbed to $228.7/mt in Jul 2026 from $155.1/mt in Sep 2025, a rise of about a fifth over the recent window. Southern and central Europe's summer drought has run deep enough that scientists are using the word desertification, with rivers far down and hardened soils leaving each dry year starting deeper in deficit.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple calorie for more than half the planet. It is thinly traded relative to how much is eaten, so a single exporter's ban or a poor monsoon moves it — and household food bills across Asia and West Africa move after it.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen 16% over the series, and is well below its Sep 2024 high of 555.1 $/mt after bottoming at 330.6 in Oct 2025. The input does not explain the move.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in every grid, motor, transformer and building. Demand for it tracks construction and electrification, and supply is concentrated in a handful of mining countries.
copper.recent: Copper has risen roughly 46% over the series, reaching $13,550/mt in Jun 2026 from a low of $8,910 in Dec 2024. The demand side is visible in the grid: AI power loads are driving new transformer designs, and electric vehicles are straining voltage on distribution networks. On the supply side Zambia, a major producer, reelected Hakainde Hichilema as it works through debt restructuring.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the price at which the world's largest borrower funds itself. It is the reference rate under mortgages, corporate loans and asset prices everywhere, so when it rises the cost of borrowing rises with it.
us-10y.recent: Yields have climbed through the summer as Treasury's sanctions campaign and a contested Fed succession pulled at the market at once: Bessent's "Economic Outcast" programme extended dollar-clearing penalties to third-country banks, and Warsh's Jackson Hole debut repriced expectations for the path of rates. The thirty-year reached 5.3%, a 2007 level.

sp500.standing: The main gauge of large-cap US equities, tracking about 500 of the biggest companies listed in America. Most retirement money in the country is indexed to it, so it doubles as the world's default measure of corporate profitability.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its Aug 13 high of 7799 after a summer led by chip and AI capital spending — Nvidia pledged $500 billion to its own buyers, financing the demand it books as revenue. Walmart's results knocked retail shares on Aug 20, and Fed minutes showed many officials saying rate hikes may be needed.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq, weighted by market value and dominated by a handful of chipmakers and platform firms. It is the closest thing to a price on the technology trade.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits below its early-June high after a July trough, and the tape since has been driven by the largest constituents rather than the broad list: Nvidia beat and guided to $108bn in revenue for next quarter, then put $3.5 billion of convertible bonds into MediaTek, whose shares rose 10%. Meta absorbed a $17.1bn child-safety settlement, roughly 1% of its stock value, and the FTC sued Amazon over its ad auction.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price a US driver pays at the pump, sampled weekly across the country. It follows crude, but refining capacity and taxes set the gap — and it is the price most Americans feel a policy or a war through first.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining, not crude, has driven the fuel story: Ukrainian drones struck Samara's oil refinery, Moscow capped station sales at 30 litres, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved." The US price has drifted down against that, easing to $4.085 from its $4.146 high on Jun 8.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas at the Dutch TTF hub, the benchmark for gas traded across Europe. It sets what utilities, heavy industry and households ultimately pay for heat and power, and it moves on pipeline supply, storage levels and competition for seaborne LNG cargoes.
natgas-ttf.recent: The move follows a squeeze on European supply: EU storage sits near 64%, well below where it should be heading into winter, and Europe is bidding against Asian buyers for the same LNG cargoes. That competition has passed through beyond Europe, with Delhi raising compressed natural gas ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option premiums. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of market fear.
vix.recent: The index has drifted down about 8% over the window and sits near the low of 14.25 reached on 14 August, well below the 22.22 peak of 10 June. The feed does not identify what drove the decline.

fx-pkr.standing: Pakistan's currency, quoted as rupees per US dollar. It sets the local price of everything the country buys abroad — fuel, gas cargoes, medicine, fertiliser — and a weaker rupee shows up in household bills long before it shows up in politics.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee drifted to its weakest of the month, 278.8 on Aug 31, with the import bill doing the pushing: Pakistan apologised for night-time blackouts after an RLNG cargo delay, and oil marketing companies keep building fuel pumps rather than chargers, leaving transport tied to imported fuel. Households at the margin are already substituting cheaper food.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the dollar. Nigeria imports most of its refined fuel and much of its food, so the naira's level sets domestic prices, and oil earnings in dollars are what the state has to defend it with.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has firmed to 1,338 from its 1,365 high on Aug 8, with foreign reserves hitting a 20-year high Friday and Moody's rewarding Abuja's austerity. FTSE Russell will reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified on September 21, restoring frontier status. Petrol imports still ran at 43% of supply in July.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the dollar. The pound sets the price of a country that imports most of its wheat and fuel, and its rate is the single number Egyptian households, importers and foreign bondholders all read.
fx-egp.recent: The pound slid to 50.88 on Aug 20 and has stayed near that level, after the United States cut off a major Egyptian bank from the global financial system on Aug 28 — part of the same push targeting banks in the UAE over Iran ties. Cairo has been leaning on debt markets, accounting for nearly half of Africa's sukuk issuance.

fx-try.standing: The value of Turkey's currency against the dollar. A country that imports most of its energy and much of its industrial input pays for both in dollars, so the lira's level sets the price of everything from fuel to food inside Turkey and the cost of its foreign debt.
fx-try.recent: The lira reached 48.28 on Sep 1, the weakest point in the month, drifting steadily from 47.54 on Aug 3 rather than moving on any single shock. Turkey spent the period in security commitments abroad — a Somali operation, a summons of Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships, and the first Istanbul committee meeting of the Mecca defence pact.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka against the US dollar. It sets the import bill for a country that buys its fuel, wheat and cotton abroad and pays for them in dollars, while its garment exports and worker remittances are what earn those dollars back.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka held in a narrow band, near 123 to the dollar, ranging only between 124 on Aug 7 and 122 on Aug 19. Nothing in the month's news — the election of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as president, the confirmed purchase of Chinese J-10CE fighters — moved it beyond that range.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupiah. It is the price of Southeast Asia's largest economy, and it sets the cost of the fuel, food and dollar debt Indonesia imports.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah strengthened from 18,040 on Aug 4 to 17,650 by Aug 21 and has held near that level since. The month's Indonesian news was structural rather than monetary: Prabowo's tightening grip on the economy through cooperatives, the captive coal plants powering the Morowali nickel smelters, and RCEP's unclosed capital gap. None of it explains the move in the rate.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Lebanon's economy runs largely on dollars, so the rate sets the real value of salaries, savings and imported food and fuel for anyone paid in local currency.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound drifted from 89,250 on Aug 3 to 89,980 on Aug 31, a slow slide against the dollar rather than a break. It moved through a month in which Lebanon's health ministry put the death toll from Israeli attacks at 4,350, Israeli strikes killed 11, and troops occupied Christian villages in the border zone.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the dollar, managed by the People's Bank of China within a daily trading band. It prices the world's largest exporter, so it sets the dollar cost of Chinese goods and the competitive pressure felt by every rival manufacturer.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan firmed steadily through the month, reaching its strongest level of the window on Sep 1 as China's factory gauge rose to 51.5 in August. Washington used the same week to ask the G20 to press Beijing to shrink its export surplus and consume more at home, a coalition-building step aimed at tariff coordination.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate of India's currency against the US dollar, the price at which the world's most populous economy pays for its imports. Oil, which India buys almost entirely from abroad, is invoiced in dollars, so the rupee sets the domestic fuel bill.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee firmed to its 30-day strongest after India's June-quarter growth came in at 7.8%, above the RBI's 7% estimate. Modi met Putin at the SCO summit in Bishkek, where India — Russia's second-largest oil buyer — keeps buying discounted crude that holds down its dollar import bill.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker real. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and its level sets the domestic price of imported fuel, fertiliser and machinery for Latin America's largest economy.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened across the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a high of 5.222 on Aug 15, and sits near 5.183. The collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe put Brazilian supervisory failure in front of investors, while Petrobras's Amazon oil find offered a longer-dated offset that has not yet moved the currency.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between Mexico's peso and the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends the large majority of its exports to the United States, so the rate tracks the health of that trade relationship.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened about 1.8% across the month, from 17.32 per dollar on Aug 3 to 16.92 on Aug 21 before settling near 17. Nothing in the window explains the move: the cross-border news it might have tracked concerned Canada's trade fight with Trump, not Mexico.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro against the US dollar, quoted here inverted as euros per dollar. It is the second-most traded currency pair in the world, and the rate at which the eurozone's trade, debt and reserves are priced against the dollar bloc.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted lower across the month, hitting its weakest point on Aug 20 before a partial recovery. Little in the period explains the move directly: the news out of Brussels ran to regulation and borders rather than rates — ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox designated very large platforms, Italy renewing its Schengen suspension with Spain, and EU gas storage sitting near 64% ahead of winter.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, and one of the most heavily traded in the world. Quoted as yen per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker yen — which lifts the cost of every barrel, cargo and component Japan imports.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen fell past 160 per dollar, a level that puts the Ministry of Finance on intervention watch — selling reserves to buy yen. The engine is the Bank of Japan's rate gap with the Fed, which spot intervention does not close, and it lands while Japanese importers and households are already paying for energy in dollars.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, and the cleanest live price on how much the outside world will still transact with Moscow. Sanctions, oil receipts and central-bank policy all land here first.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened through August as Russia's oil leverage thinned: a Georgian refinery at Kulevi took its first Libyan cargo in place of Russian crude, and Washington signalled fresh bank designations while Germany prepared national sanctions. Against that, Siluanov's return to the G20 table brought recognition but no relief, with Bessent tying any easing to the war's end.

fx-zar.standing: The rand against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies and a standing proxy for risk appetite towards Africa. It moves with commodity prices, domestic politics and global rate expectations, and it sets the import bill for fuel.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through August, from 16.52 on Aug 4 to a low of 15.92 on Aug 26, but the currency's strength did not reach the pump: petrol still rises R1.34 a litre on Tuesday, because the fuel formula passes through a war premium the exchange rate cannot offset.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency, traded around the clock against the dollar with no central issuer and a fixed supply schedule. Its price is the market's clearest read on appetite for risk outside the banking system.
btc.recent: The rally from $62,840 on Aug 17 was a short squeeze rather than fresh leverage: open interest collapsed as Bitcoin surged to $80,020 on Aug 25, up 23.7% that week. Traders had been pricing Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, and BlackRock cut its in-kind swap threshold from $25 million to $1 million on Aug 26.

eth.standing: The unit of account on the Ethereum network, the largest platform for programmable contracts and the settlement layer beneath most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised trading venues. Demand for block space and for collateral moves it.
eth.recent: Ether climbed with the rest of the majors after Treasury buybacks lifted risk appetite in mid-August, and the rally held through a run of favourable Washington news: the SEC proposed its first major crypto rule in a surprise announcement, and Trump pushed Congress to move on the Clarity Act. The peak came on Aug 22.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by a physical gold bar, so its price tracks an ounce of bullion. Gold is what buyers hold when they distrust currencies, banks or governments, which makes its price a running measure of that distrust.
paxg.recent: Gold's climb ran alongside a test of Federal Reserve independence, with bitcoin and gold pricing Warsh's Jackson Hole speech before the late-August peak. The metal's role outside the financial system showed elsewhere: Islamic State buried $47 million in gold and cash in Deir ez-Zor, and Kassala street dealers outbid Sudan's licensed market.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: The field of building machines that perform tasks associated with human reasoning — learning, language, perception. It is both a research programme and, now, an industry whose costs, chips and labour effects are argued over in public.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Attention tracked a fortnight of institutional fights over who controls the technology. A US court ruled the Pentagon's ban of Anthropic unlawful, calling it "illegal and baseless"; the EU placed ChatGPT under its stricter platform rules alongside Reddit and Roblox; and Bill Gates reversed his January position on job losses.

wiki-russia.standing: The daily count of people reading the English Wikipedia article on Russia. It rises when the country moves into the news, and the shape of the curve marks which days carried the events that sent readers looking.
wiki-russia.recent: Readership climbed through a month in which Russia was the actor in several stories at once: a strike on an arms depot near Kyiv whose stored shells detonated and killed 37, Niger's generals asking Moscow to put down their army's mutiny and thanking Africa Corps in person, and Washington bringing finance minister Anton Siluanov back to the G20 table over European objection.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up. It rises when something there breaks into the global news cycle and settles back within days.

wiki-china.standing: The Wikipedia article on China, and the daily count of people reading it. It is a rough gauge of where general public curiosity lands — the article a reader opens when a country turns up in a headline and they want the background rather than the news.
wiki-china.recent: Readership tracked a run of China stories: Vietnam demanded Beijing halt construction on two Paracel features, Bangladesh confirmed a deal for China's J-10CE fighters, and new hangars at the Malan flight-test base showed what aircraft China expects to fly. Washington then asked the G20 to press Beijing to curb its export surplus.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The narrow sea lane between Iran and Oman that connects the Gulf to open ocean, and the only way out for the oil and LNG loaded on its shores. About a fifth of the world's crude passes through it, so its width is a permanent constraint on global supply.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership followed the closure fight. Iran declared that transit requires Tehran's permission and the IRGC claimed a veto, leaving 6,000 sailors stranded aboard anchored ships; CENTCOM countered that the lanes were open, citing 7 tankers on Thursday. US strikes on Larak Island and a supertanker hitting mines kept the strait contested.

wiki-india.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on India — a rough gauge of when the world's most populous country pulls outside attention, and which of its stories travel beyond its own press.
wiki-india.recent: The 15 August peak fell on India's Independence Day. Readership held up through a week in which Modi met Putin in Bishkek and pressed for peace in Ukraine while India remained one of the largest buyers of discounted Russian crude, and Delhi reported 7.8% June-quarter growth, above the RBI's own estimate. Flash floods on the Nepal border left 288 Indians missing.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine. It rises and falls with the war's news cycle, and works as a rough gauge of how much of the world is paying attention on any given day.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak came as Ukraine's allies convened in Kyiv and Zelenskyy said Patriot deliveries have halved since 2023, alongside Britain letting MBDA share SCALP missile component data with France and Ukraine. Attention held through the Kyiv-area depot blast that killed 37 and Zaporizhzhia's week on diesel power.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed to 3 vessels a day, about half the 90-day baseline, as the US struck Larak Island and Tehran declared that transit now requires its permission. A supertanker was stopped after hitting mines in the strait, and 6,000 sailors remain stuck aboard anchored ships while Brent trades at $90.97.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits about a tenth below its 90-day baseline after a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, the same day Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Yemen's Saada. Daily transits bottomed at 14 on 5 August, down from 47 in early June, with seas calm throughout.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Transits are running only a few percent above their 90-day baseline, with the Aug 11 high of 57 vessels a day still well short of normal. Houthi attacks continue: a vessel was struck off Saudi Arabia on Aug 24, and Pakistani nationals injured in an earlier Red Sea attack returned home.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has drifted down through the window, from 264 vessels a day on Jun 22 to 192, running about 8.5% below its own 90-day baseline with calm seas and no weather alert. The coverage does not explain the decline.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic is running close to its 90-day baseline despite a crowded diplomatic week around it: Washington used the G20 to press other nations to act against China's export surplus, Vietnam demanded China halt construction on two Paracel features, and Nvidia took a $3.5 billion stake option in Taipei's MediaTek. None of it has moved the ships.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits are down about 13% against their own 90-day baseline, and the Panama Canal moved to cap daily transits in anticipation of a severe El Niño — the dry phase that drains the lake feeding the locks. Traffic has run near 28 vessels a day since the 83-transit high on 13 July.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic sits near the low end of its 82-day range after a run of attacks on shipping: a third Greek vessel in three days burned in the Black Sea on 18 August, and Turkey summoned Kyiv's ambassador on 30 August over strikes on its own ships. Daily transits bottomed at 38 on 16 August, against a high of 100 on 9 June.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic held near its own baseline through the summer, peaking at 163 vessels on Jun 13 and bottoming at 112 on Jun 3. The disruption around the strait has been at the border rather than on the water: Italy extended its suspension of Schengen free movement with Spain to September 15, a month after the Ceuta migrant crossings.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic sits near its 82-day average, about 6% below the 90-day baseline, with calm water and no weather alert. The swing between the 1 August high of 186 vessels and the 3 August low of 126 came and went without a closure in the record.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic held near the top of its range as attacks on shipping kept crews off the Red Sea route: a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, and a third Greek vessel in three days burned in the Black Sea. Rough seas and 3.2m waves have since met the diverted traffic.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, roughly 97% below its own 90-day baseline, with the last reading of 25 vessels on 4 June and the first empty day on 17 July. Turkey summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships in the Black Sea, and shipping has been pricing war risk across the region — Moscow now pitches its Trans-Arctic corridor as the alternative route.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits near the bottom of a 35-day slide, down roughly 3% from its Jun 16 high of 11,150 to a Jul 15 low of 10,700. Riyadh spent August signing a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey, shelling villages in Yemen's Razih district, and awaiting US congressional review of a nuclear deal tied to recognition of Israel.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a low on Jul 30, with a 1.7% fall on the latest day. Istanbul hosted the first committee meeting under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement on Aug 31, with Pakistan sending Deputy PM Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and army chief Asim Munir; Turkey also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on its ships.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index has drifted down from its Jun 18 high of 6270 as the war reached the UAE directly: two Iranian ballistic missiles triggered Dubai's first emergency alert in months on 18 August, the UAE suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran the same week, and on 31 August it downed an Iranian drone over its territorial waters.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index slipped from its Aug 26 high of 1749 after prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri with concealing some $40 million in assets on Aug 27, reviving the political-risk discount Malaysian equities carried through the last asset-concealment case. It still sits above its Jul 1 low of 1657.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed through a stretch in which Prabowo tightened the state's grip on the economy, with one president's imprint now running policy from cooperatives outward. The downstreaming push behind the nickel boom continues to build smelter capacity in Morowali and Central Sulawesi, powered by captive coal plants outside the national grid.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index has drifted lower as the yen fell past 160 per dollar, putting the Ministry of Finance on intervention watch and raising the cost of energy for Japanese importers and households. The Bank of Japan's rate gap with the Fed is the engine behind the currency move. Nissan and Honda signed a vehicle-software deal on 31 August.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index has drifted lower across the window despite China's factory gauge rising to 51.5 in August, a gain concentrated in AI capital spending rather than broad demand. Washington spent the week rallying the G20 to press Beijing to curb its export surplus, the opening move in tariff coordination that would land on exactly these listed exporters.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits near the middle of its range, roughly 4% below the June high, with an August factory gauge at 51.5 pointing to expansion but concentrated in AI capital spending rather than broad demand. Washington is separately pressing the G20 to make China curb its export surplus and lift domestic consumption.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The Bank of Korea hiked rates to 3.00% on 27 August, tightening into a chip cycle rather than against inflation, and the index has given up more than a fifth since its 22 June high of 9115. Politics added noise: Lee named Lee Hyoung-il finance minister, and Washington scrapped the Twin Dragons exercise.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits well above its June low after India's economy grew 7.8% in the June quarter, beating forecasts. Bank leadership is in flux: HDFC Bank's CEO declined a third term. Delhi has meanwhile kept buying Russian crude as Modi met Putin, leaving India's fuel bill outside the Western sanctions track.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed steadily since June, reaching 5,768 on Aug 17 before easing. Singapore's role as a trade and finance conduit ran through the period: a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties, and crypto card spending in the city tripled to $1.04 billion.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index rose as Nvidia bought into MediaTek through $3.5 billion in convertible bonds, sending MediaTek shares up 10% and lifting the Taipei chip complex with them. The gain came despite Taiwan indicting nine people, including an Nvidia manager, over AI server smuggling the week before.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the middle of a narrow 34-day band between 1541 on Jun 23 and 1639 on Jul 17, and fell 2.4% on the day. Nothing in the record explains the drop; Bangkok's news in the window ran to Thailand's approach to Russia on cybersecurity cooperation and trade talk, neither of which is a market event.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index fell about 5% in a day to 6,074, giving back much of a run that had carried it from 5,799 on 1 June to a 6,404 peak on 17 July. Nothing in the available material accounts for the drop.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing from its June low, but the domestic picture underneath it has turned: home prices in Sydney fell for a fifth straight month, and homebuyer numbers have collapsed. KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff in late August, and Iran's threat to close Hormuz hangs over the energy import bill.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index has climbed over the window, reaching a high on Aug 21 before easing. Domestic news has run to fiscal and governance stories rather than market ones: Treasury moving on R88.6bn in unclaimed accounts and pensions, and the disclosure that Dlomo diverted 12 million rand into covert operations.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index fell to its series low of 166,300 on 18 August before recovering, and the domestic financial news since has been a bank failure: Bank Master collapsed in a fraud probe that exposed supervisory failures in Brasília. Against that, Lula has been promoting new Amazon oil, with Petrobras detecting signs of crude off the Amazon coast.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down about 4% over the past 65 days, from its Jun 2 high of 68,890 to a Aug 18 low of 63,930, and closed at 65,430. The input names no Mexican policy or market event behind the slide.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index has drifted down about 3% over the past three months, off its 22 July high of 3,380,000 and near the 19 August low of 2,874,000. The one Buenos Aires story in the window is an Interpol operation that dismantled a fraud network, with 58 arrested and 196 identified — nothing that explains the move in equities.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index fell 1.5% to 36,270 as the trade war with the United States widened. Canada matched US tariffs dollar for dollar on 22 August and refused relief on heavy trucks, Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports, and Trump demanded Canadian companies relocate to the US.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index slipped 0.58% on the day, easing back from its Aug 13 high as the Gulf escalation widened: the US struck Iranian launchers on Larak Island on Sunday, the United Arab Emirates downed an Iranian drone offshore, and a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its two-month range after climbing from its June low, and the last session gave back a fraction of that. Energy weighting kept it supported as Brent crude rose 3% to $90.97 on the Iran strikes, a move that lifts the oil majors that dominate the index.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index sits near its 14 August high after a run of roughly 5% over the window, with the pull toward European security. Merz plans to blame Russia for the Leipzig drone incident and Berlin is preparing sanctions, while Croatia's arrest of a second Nord Stream suspect keeps the pipeline case open.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Paris-listed defence and space names have had a run of contract news: Sweden signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates from Naval Group, and the European Space Agency awarded €544 million to three rocket startups. The index sits below its Aug 10 high of 8726 but well above the Jun 1 low of 8147.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index has climbed to 1106, roughly 7% above its Jun 1 low of 1036, and sits a little below the Aug 13 high of 1120. The most direct pressure on the listed energy names came late in the window, with EU gas storage hitting a record low on 2026-08-29.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed roughly a tenth over the past three months, from a low of 18,140 on Jun 10 to a peak of 20,210 on Aug 11, and sits near that high. Nothing in the recent Spanish news — Italy's renewed 15-day suspension of Schengen border checks with Spain, or the Bronze Age museum theft — accounts for the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index has climbed about 5.7% over the window, reaching 53,720 on Aug 7 before easing to 52,610. Little in the period speaks directly to Milan: the domestic news is Rome's renewed suspension of Schengen free movement with Spain, extending border checks on travellers and freight between two EU founding members to September 15.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index is roughly 7% higher across the window, peaking at 14,630 on Aug 10 before easing to 14,290. Nothing in the available material explains the move: the Zurich stories in the window concern a percolation proof from the city's mathematicians and Russia's stated loss of trust in Switzerland as a talks venue.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range, well above the June low. Stockholm signed a €4.3 billion contract for four Naval Group frigates on 31 August — roughly €1.1 billion per hull — money flowing to a French yard rather than a Swedish one.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index sits at 4,057, down about 4% across the past 64 days from its 12 June high of 4,292 and near the 29 June low of 3,966. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever officials signal a shift in how they read inflation and jobs.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and the market for no change climbed to 75 on Aug 15 before falling back to 43. The Jackson Hole speech by Warsh on 28 August was itself being priced by bitcoin and gold, a sign of how much the path now rests on the Fed's independence.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the 47th president of the United States, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with what he does, which makes it a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention American politics is holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The peak on Aug 26 came in a week built around Iran: Trump posted about Iran 319 times as his stated war aims shifted, declared the Strait of Hormuz clear, and posted a fake video of the Kharg Island oil terminal exploding. Brent rose 3% to $90.97 on strikes. He also asked regulators to punish NBC anchor Kristen Welker.

wiki-stablecoin.standing: A crypto token pegged to a national currency, usually the dollar, and backed by reserves held off-chain. It is the settlement layer most crypto trading runs on, and the form in which banks, card networks and payment firms are now moving deposits.
wiki-stablecoin.recent: Banks moved onto the rails rather than around them: Shinhan began building won stablecoin rails with a card network, Standard Chartered started distributing Hong Kong's dollar stablecoin, and 39 state banking associations announced a rival chain. Crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion, and one paper puts $700 billion of bank lending capacity at risk.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States — a broad attention gauge that rises when the country itself, rather than any single institution, becomes the subject of a story people want background on.
wiki-united-states.recent: The rise tracked a widening US–Iran exchange: US forces struck Iranian launchers on Larak Island on Sunday, Iran struck two US airbases in Jordan, and the UAE downed an Iranian drone offshore. Washington unveiled "Operation Economic Outcast" the Monday before the Aug 28 peak, and photos of Maduro in US detention circulated alongside it.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The number of people reading the Bitcoin article on Wikipedia each day — a rough gauge of how far the asset has travelled beyond the people who already hold it, and one that rises when a price move or a shock reaches a general audience.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The 24 August peak followed a run to $80,020, up 23.7% in a week, that turned out to be a short squeeze rather than a leveraged rally; the basis trade paid market makers who took no view on price. BlackRock cut its swap-in threshold from $25 million to $1 million, and Rakbank Islamic opened Bitcoin trading on its shariah-compliant platform.

wiki-nepal.standing: Daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Nepal, a Himalayan state of roughly 30 million wedged between India and China, whose rivers drain the world's highest mountains into narrow, densely settled valleys.
wiki-nepal.recent: A flash flood tore down the Bhotekoshi from the Nepal-China border on 26 August without rain falling first, and the toll has climbed from 160 to over 5,000, with 934 workers trapped or missing at hydropower sites. A second burst in Tibet and a barrier lake holding 2 million cubic metres behind a landslide dam forced rescuers in Rasuwa to flee.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve targets for overnight lending between banks. It is the base price of dollar credit: mortgages, corporate borrowing and the value of the dollar against every other currency reprice off it.
fed-funds.recent: The target has sat at 3.75% since December 2025, down from 5% in September 2024, but the direction of travel has flipped. Minutes released on 19 August showed many officials saying rate hikes may be needed, and by Warsh's Jackson Hole debut markets favored a September hike.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks to park cash with it overnight, and the floor under euro-area borrowing costs. It sets what savers earn, what mortgages cost and how the euro trades against the dollar.
ecb-rate.recent: The rate has come down over the series, from 3.50% to 2.25%, and sits above the 2.00% low reached in June 2025. The input does not explain the latest move; elsewhere the direction has turned, with the Bank of Korea hiking to 3.00% and Fed minutes showing many officials said rate hikes may be needed.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans who want work and cannot find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when it sets interest rates, and the one voters feel first.
us-unemployment.recent: The rate stands at 4.1%, unchanged over the window and near the bottom of its recent range — down from the 4.5% high of November 2025, and just above the 4.0% low of January 2025. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer, where a small state budget rests on crude exports and a naira that moves with them. Its elections, fuel prices and security shape West Africa's economy and migration.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Readership held near its highest point in early August around the fuel-subsidy fight: Atiku Abubakar vowed to restore Nigeria's petrol subsidy if elected in 2027, and the APC accused him of desperation. Attention has drifted down since, through Moody's rewarding austerity as foreign reserves hit a 20-year high and FTSE Russell's move to reclassify Nigeria as frontier.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A prediction market on which party wins the most seats in Russia's State Duma election. United Russia is the party that has held a governing majority since the chamber's modern form, so the contract is less a race than a measure of how firmly that arrangement holds.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The contract drifted up from 64 on Aug 3 to a high of 75 on Aug 30, as the war removed any opening for a domestic challenge: Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead, Russia claimed it destroyed Ukraine's Flamingo missile plants, and Modi's call at Bishkek for the war to end came without leverage attached.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington lifts its naval and economic blockade of Iran by a set date. It is priced by traders putting money on the outcome, so it moves with the fighting and with the state of talks rather than with any official signal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The odds collapsed from 86% on Aug 8 to 20% as the war widened rather than wound down: the US struck Larak Island, Iran said Hormuz transit now requires Tehran's permission, and Jordan intercepted eight missiles over its airspace. Treasury is preparing a further bank designation, and Brent rose 3% to $90.97.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States mounts a ground invasion of Iran. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for it happening — a running read on how much of an escalation the market is willing to back with money.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The price has fallen through a month of strikes that stayed short of invasion. The US hit two Iranian launchers on Larak Island on Sunday and Tehran retaliated, and Brent rose 3% to $90.97 — a war premium, not a supply loss. Washington's pressure has run through sanctions instead: Treasury will designate another bank without naming it.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A prediction market on whether Israel and Iran will be under a ceasefire by a set date. It prices what traders will pay for the outcome, so it moves on strikes, talks and sanctions rather than on any official assessment.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Odds slid to 63 on Aug 10 and have since climbed back toward the high, even as the fighting widened: the US struck Larak Island on Sunday, Tehran said it retaliated, Jordan downed eight missiles in its airspace and the UAE shot down an Iranian drone offshore. Brent rose 3% to $90.97 on the exchanges.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election, priced as a percentage. It is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll — and it reprices on candidacy rulings, endorsements and court decisions rather than on survey fieldwork.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The contract rose from 25% on Aug 2 to a high of 41% on Aug 31. The input carries no Brazilian political news explaining the repricing; the surrounding coverage concerns prediction markets themselves, including a Ninth Circuit ruling curbing Kalshi and a White House aide fined for betting on speeches.

xag.standing: The price of an ounce of silver, an industrial and monetary metal at once: it is consumed in solar panels, electronics and brazing alloys, and bought as a store of value, so it moves on both factory demand and financial panic.
xag.recent: The series more than doubled off its $29.81 low on Aug 6 to a $69.42 peak on Aug 28, and no supply, policy or demand event in the input explains the move.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The refined and unrefined liquid hydrocarbon that fuels most transport and feeds the chemicals industry. Who controls the reserves, and who is allowed to sell them, decides far more than the price at the pump.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Attention followed the seizure of Venezuela's reserves: Washington negotiated a stake in Venezuelan oil in late August, and 65 billion barrels changed hands on Friday 29 August through a vehicle named North American Blue Energy Partners, with Maduro in US detention. Brent then rose 3% to $90.97 on strikes on Iran.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marco Rubio wins the 2028 US presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on party positioning and the field of rivals, not on any single poll.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.recent: The contract drifted from 13% on Aug 2 to 10% on Aug 31 with no news about Rubio behind it. What moved around the venue instead was regulation and trust: the Ninth Circuit ruled sports bets aren't "swaps," South Korea joined more than 30 jurisdictions restricting Polymarket access, and a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine over bets on the president's speeches.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro places second in Brazil's presidential race. Traders buy and sell shares that pay out if the outcome happens, so the price reads as the going rate on that result rather than anyone's stated forecast.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.recent: The contract has held in a narrow band, moving from 80 on Aug 2 to 88 on Aug 6 and staying near the top of that range since. Nothing in the window explains the shift: the Polymarket news of the period concerned the platform itself — 152 wallets showing a 97.2% win rate, and South Korea joining more than 30 jurisdictions restricting access.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether J.D. Vance becomes the Republican nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reprices on party standing, rivals entering or leaving, and the incumbent's reach.
poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-republic.recent: The contract sat near its low of 43 on Aug 8 and climbed to 49 by Aug 30, a stretch in which the venue itself was the news: a White House aide paid a fine over bets placed on the president's speeches after reading them early, and the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports bets aren't "swaps," confirming state powers over prediction markets.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Gavin Newsom becomes the Democratic presidential nominee in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on party manoeuvring rather than on any vote yet held.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.recent: The contract drifted from 19% on Aug 2 to 14% on Aug 25 without a candidate event behind it, while the venues themselves took the news. The Ninth Circuit ruled sports bets aren't "swaps," Connecticut sued Kalshi, and a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine over bets on Trump's speeches.

poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.standing: A market where traders buy and sell contracts on whether the US Federal Reserve will raise its policy rate this year. The price is what people are paying for that outcome, and it moves as rate-setters speak and inflation data lands.
poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.recent: Odds climbed from 46 on Aug 16 to 72, with the jump following Fed minutes on Aug 19 showing many officials said rate hikes may be needed. Warsh's Jackson Hole speech kept the question live, with bitcoin and gold pricing it in.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Édouard Philippe, the former French prime minister who now leads his own centre-right party, wins the presidency. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of candidates forms.
poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.recent: The contract has barely moved in a month, holding at 26% with a high of 26 on Aug 2 and a low of 25 on Aug 24. Nothing in the window bears on the French race; the news around Polymarket concerned the platform itself, including South Korea joining more than 30 jurisdictions restricting access.

poly-next-mythos-class-model-released-by.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a specific outcome occurs by a set date, priced in cents on the dollar. The price is what traders will pay for the bet, not a forecast — it moves as money changes hands on new information.
poly-next-mythos-class-model-released-by.recent: Prediction markets themselves spent the week under legal and regulatory pressure. The Ninth Circuit ruled on 28 August that sports bets are not "swaps", confirming state powers over Kalshi, Connecticut filed a further suit, and a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine to settle an insider-trading case over bets on the president's speeches.

poly-will-renan-santos-finish-in-third-p.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Renan Santos finishes third in a Brazilian election field. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with candidate news rather than with any official count.
poly-will-renan-santos-finish-in-third-p.recent: The contract has fallen by about three quarters from its 65% high on Aug 10 to 16%, with no event in the input explaining the slide.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Avigdor Lieberman, the Israeli politician who leads the secular-nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party, becomes Israel's next prime minister. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The contract has barely moved in a month, trading between 4% and 6% and ending where it started. Nothing in the period touched the question of who leads Israel: the news was the conduct of the war — strikes in Gaza and Jenin, the occupation of Christian villages in south Lebanon, and Israeli strikes on a Syrian air base.

poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel shuts its airspace to civil aviation before a set date. Traders price it as a proxy for how close the region is to a war wide enough to ground flights over Tel Aviv, so it moves with escalation rather than with fighting itself.
poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.recent: The price has halved from its 12% peak on Aug 19, when eight strikes hit an airbase in Syria's Idlib and a Trump envoy said the US had no notice. Since then Israeli operations have stayed local — a home struck in Jenin, a hospital compound in Gaza, a car in Beit Jinn — and traders have priced out a wider war.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract on the party split of the next US Congress, paying out if Republicans hold both the Senate and the House after the 2026 midterms. It prices one of four possible chamber combinations, so it moves as traders shift weight between them.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.recent: The market barely moved, holding between 12% on Aug 6 and 14% on Aug 15 before settling at 13%. What moved in the same window was the venue rather than the odds: a Ninth Circuit ruling confirmed state powers over prediction markets, Connecticut sued Kalshi, South Korea restricted Polymarket access, and a White House teleprompter operator paid a fine over bets on the president's speeches.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a specific US crypto market-structure bill becomes law before the year is out. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, so it tracks the bill's odds of clearing Congress and being signed rather than its merits.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The slide from 34% on Aug 2 to 14% tracked a run of legal and scandal news around prediction markets and crypto regulation: the Ninth Circuit ruled on Aug 28 that Kalshi's sports bets aren't "swaps," confirming state powers, Connecticut filed its own suit a day earlier, and a White House teleprompter operator settled an insider-trading probe over bets on Trump's speeches.

stocks:AMP.AX.standing: A listed Australian wealth manager and bank, running superannuation, advice and retirement products for retail savers. Its earnings track fund flows and the value of the assets it manages, so it moves with the savings cycle rather than with any single market.
stocks:AMP.AX.recent: The shares climbed from their Aug 3 low of 2.12 to 2.43 on Sep 1, a gain of about 15% across the window. The one story in the record — Sydney home prices falling for a fifth straight month against a rate wall — bears on the Australian savings and lending backdrop, but nothing in the input explains the move in this stock.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The shares of the company whose accelerators do most of the world's AI training and inference. Its order book is the closest thing to a meter on AI capital spending, and its suppliers, customers and financiers are priced off it.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The 27 August high followed two disclosures: quarterly earnings that beat estimates with guidance to $108bn in revenue next quarter, and talks to buy Hugging Face at above $13 billion. The same weeks brought scrutiny of Nvidia's role as lender to its own market — a $500 billion pledge to buyers and $230 billion in backstopped lease obligations.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves when a rival gains ground, a candidate declares, or a party's field shifts.
poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.recent: The contract drifted from 9% on Aug 2 to 7% on Aug 13 and sits at 8%, a move without a clear trigger in the field. What news there was concerned the venue rather than the race: the Ninth Circuit ruled sports bets aren't "swaps", confirming state powers over prediction markets, and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-will-1-fed-rate-cut-happen-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve cuts its policy rate at least once during 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the rate path looks looser or tighter.
poly-will-1-fed-rate-cut-happen-in-2026.recent: The contract sits near the bottom of its range after Fed minutes showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, leaving a cut priced as remote. Attention around the venue itself has been on Kalshi, where the Ninth Circuit ruled sports bets aren't "swaps," and on a White House aide fined for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will still hold the Israeli premiership after the next change of government. Traders price the survival of a coalition, so it moves on scandal, war, and the arithmetic of Knesset defections rather than on polling alone.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: The contract slid from 37% on Aug 2 to 25% on Aug 28 as Israel widened operations on several fronts and drew external rebukes: strikes on a Syrian air base the US said it was not warned about, an airstrike on a home under construction in Jenin, a raid on an UNRWA training centre in occupied East Jerusalem, and Turkey's move to seek an Interpol notice for Netanyahu over the Gaza flotilla case.

poly-iran-full-airspace-closure-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran shuts its airspace to civil aviation by a set date. Traders price it as a percentage, and it rises when the region looks closer to open war, because a closed airspace reroutes long-haul traffic across Asia and Europe.
poly-iran-full-airspace-closure-by-septe.recent: The odds have collapsed from 52% on Aug 2 to 8%, holding near their Aug 27 low of 6% even as the fighting widened: the US struck Larak Island, Jordan downed eight missiles, and the UAE shot down an Iranian drone offshore. Tehran's escalation has run through Hormuz shipping and permission regimes rather than its own skies.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve holds its policy rate flat through the whole of 2026. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for a no-cut year — and it moves as the case for easing strengthens or fades.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, leaving no room for cuts, and the price has sat near the top of its range since. It touched 89 on 2 August and its low of 85 on 9 August. Warsh's Jackson Hole speech was the month's other Fed event.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come to blows within a set window. It prices how close traders think the war in Ukraine is to spilling across an alliance border — the line between a regional war and an Article 5 one.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The odds fell after the peak on Aug 27, the day Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead and four EU states reopened the debate on Russia's frozen billions. Since then the escalation has stayed inside Ukraine and Russia — the depot blast near Kyiv, the Belgorod strike, Zaporizhzhia on diesel — and at Bishkek Modi pressed Putin for dialogue over battlefield solutions.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A prediction market on whether crude oil sets a new record price within a set window. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, so it moves with anything that threatens supply, and it is one of the fastest reads on how seriously the market takes a shock.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: The contract drifted down from 14% on Aug 2 to 12%, with a low of 10% on Aug 9, and the input carries no oil supply event to explain it. What moved around Polymarket instead was scrutiny of prediction markets themselves: South Korea joined more than 30 jurisdictions restricting access.

stocks:RDDT.standing: Shares in the company behind Reddit, the link-and-comment forum network whose thousands of user-run communities make it one of the largest discussion platforms on the open web and a major supplier of training text and search results.
stocks:RDDT.recent: Reddit crossed 45 million average monthly EU users and was designated a Very Large Online Platform under the Digital Services Act, alongside ChatGPT and Roblox. Designation obliges systemic-risk assessment, independent audit, an ad repository and researcher data access, with fines up to 6% of global turnover. The stock is down from 178.1 on Aug 14 to 147.8.

stocks:RBLX.standing: Shares in the company behind Roblox, an online platform where users build and play games made by other users, with an audience skewed heavily toward children and teenagers. Its exposure runs through advertising, in-game spending and child-safety regulation.
stocks:RBLX.recent: The stock rose to $41.29 on Aug 31 as the European Commission designated Roblox, alongside ChatGPT and Reddit, a Very Large Online Platform under the Digital Services Act after it crossed 45 million average monthly EU users. Designation brings systemic-risk assessment, independent audit and researcher data access, with fines up to 6% of global turnover.

stocks:HMC.standing: Shares in Japan's second-largest carmaker, listed in New York as an American depositary receipt. Honda sells more engines than any other company on earth — motorcycles, cars and generators — so the stock tracks demand across both rich and emerging markets.
stocks:HMC.recent: Honda's two-wheeler sales in India reached 579,000 units in August, up 8%. On 31 August the company signed a deal with Nissan to shorten vehicle software development cycles, a tie-up between two of Japan's largest carmakers. The shares have climbed from a low of $29.60 on Aug 3.

stocks:MARUTI.BO.standing: India's largest carmaker by volume, majority-owned by Japan's Suzuki, and the maker of most of the small hatchbacks on Indian roads. Its share price is the closest thing the market has to a read on middle-class consumer demand.
stocks:MARUTI.BO.recent: The stock has drifted down through the month to its lowest level in the series, despite August sales data pointing the other way: Honda's two-wheeler arm HMSI sold 579,000 units, up 8 per cent. The gap is between wholesale dispatches and retail demand, which the August figures do not settle.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares in the world's largest consumer-electronics maker, whose revenue still turns mostly on the iPhone and whose supply chain reaches through Chinese assembly plants. Its size makes it a heavy weight in every major US index.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple confirmed a September 9 event for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with an Ultra expected at $2,500, and announced M6 and M5 Ultra chips on August 25. Enterprise AI buyers running models locally have emptied Mac Mini and Mac Studio inventory, demand Apple did not forecast. OpenAI on Monday denied stealing Apple trade secrets.
